chunks: And from him, from Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about the fasting person who suffers from an ear ailment and pours medicine into it; he said, 'There is no harm in it.'

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: There is no harm in it (permissible)

ai.seo_question: Does putting medicine in the ear break the fast during Ramadan?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that instilling medicine into the ear does not break the fast, a ruling derived from the principle that the ear is a distinct cavity separate from the throat. This establishes a key precedent in Shia jurisprudence for distinguishing between substances that reach the stomach and those that remain in the head, reinforcing the permissibility of medical treatment during Ramadan without invalidating the fast.
